from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the N-Sphere", [
            "We define n-spheres analytically beyond visualization.",
            "Hyper-volume and surface area change with dimensions.",
            "4D glome projections reveal complex internal slices."
        ])

        # Equation setup
        equation = MathTex(
            r"x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \dots + x_n^2 = r^2",
            font_size=40,
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(equation, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # We define n-spheres analytically beyond visualization.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Write(equation))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Hyper-volume and surface area change with dimensions.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        
        # Represent hyper-volume concept
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#00CED1", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(circle, 'C2', 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        volume_label = Text("Hyper-Volume", font_size=20, color="#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(volume_label, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Create(circle), Write(volume_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # 4D glome projections reveal complex internal slices.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))
        
        # Pulse the equation
        self.play(
            equation.animate.set_color("#FF69B4").scale(1.1),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        self.play(
            equation.animate.set_color(WHITE).scale(1/1.1),
            run_time=1.0
        )

        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Mathematics allows us to explore hidden dimensions.",
            "Geometry provides consistent logic without visualization.",
            "Algebraic precision overcomes our limited intuition."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        math_symbol = MathTex(r"\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \text{geometry}_n", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(math_symbol, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)

        geometry_cloud = VGroup(*[Dot(point=np.random.randn(3)/3 + self.grid['E4'], color=TEAL) for _ in range(50)])
        combined_group = VGroup(math_symbol, geometry_cloud)
        self.place_in_area(combined_group, 'D1', 'F3', scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(math_symbol))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(geometry_cloud))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(geometry_cloud.animate.scale(1.5).set_opacity(0.3))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Scaling Dimensions
sections.content: Establish the pattern of geometric growth from 1D (line segment) to 2D (circle) and 3D (sphere) using the distance formula: x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = r².
sections.example: Visual animation showing a point expanding into a line, then a circle, then a sphere as we increment the variable 'n'.

sections.title: Defining the N-Sphere
sections.content: Introduce the hypersphere (n-sphere) in n-dimensional space. Explain that while we cannot visualize it, we can define it analytically. Focus on the concept of 'Hyper-Volume' and 'Hyper-Surface Area'.
sections.example: A 4D 'glome' representation projected into 3D, showing its cross-sections (slices) changing from points to spheres and back to points.

sections.title: The Paradox of Concentration of Measure
sections.content: Explain the counter-intuitive phenomenon: as dimensions increase, the volume of a hypersphere concentrates near its surface (the 'crust'), leaving the core virtually empty.
sections.example: An animation of an orange where, in 100 dimensions, almost 99.9% of the 'juice' (volume) is contained in the thin peel, leaving the center hollow.

sections.title: Application: Data Science and High Dimensions
sections.content: Connect the theory to real-world applications. High-dimensional spheres explain why 'Nearest Neighbor' searches fail in high-dimensional datasets (The Curse of Dimensionality).
sections.example: A digital AI character (Bot-3000) trying to find a similar image in a massive database; as the features increase, all data points seem equally far away, representing points on the shell of a high-dimensional sphere.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap the progression: Geometry is a language. Even if we cannot see 10D, the mathematics remain consistent. Emphasize that intuition breaks down, but algebraic precision survives.
sections.example: A final visual showing a 3D sphere morphing into a complex data cloud, emphasizing that mathematics is our 'eyes' in higher dimensions.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The radius label (r_label) at B4 is too close to the shape and risks overlapping with the sphere animation as it expands. Fix: Line 70: self.place_at_grid('r_label', 'B5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=70, object=r_label)
issues.resolution_note: Updated r_label positioning to B5.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The current layout does not utilize the bottom grid rows, leading to a top-heavy visual balance on the right side. Fix: self.place_in_area(group, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.85) (line=0, object=entire animation group)
issues.resolution_note: Utilized the B3-D4 area to center animations and improve visual balance.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The equation is poorly centered and isolated at B3, creating significant negative space. Fix: Line 59: self.place_in_area(equation, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2) (line=59, object=equation)
issues.resolution_note: Replaced manual placement with place_in_area at B2-B5, scaled by 1.2 as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The hyper-volume graphic and label are positioned too low in the frame (E3/F3), creating an unbalanced visual weight. Fix: Line 72: self.place_in_area(circle, 'C2', 'E4', scale_factor=1.0) (line=72, object=circle)
issues.resolution_note: Moved circle to C2-E4 area as requested to fix balance.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The volume_label is detached from its associated circle, violating proximity standards. Fix: Line 75: self.place_at_grid(volume_label, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9) (line=75, object=volume_label)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed label proximity by placing it at E3 and scaling to 0.9.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Cube/sphere animation is horizontally centered in the right grid, creating poor balance with the left-aligned text. Fix: Line 59: self.place_in_area('cube', 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=59, object=cube)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed cube positioning using place_in_area as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Visual elements at C3 are too static and visually clash with the lecture lines appearing on the left side. Fix: Line 67: self.place_in_area('sphere', 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=67, object=sphere)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed sphere positioning using place_in_area as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The orange 'crust' visualization is confined to a small center point, failing to utilize available screen real estate. Fix: Line 76: self.place_in_area('crust', 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0) (line=76, object=crust)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed crust visualization positioning using place_in_area as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The animation of scatter points (geometry_n) overlaps with the lecture text, reducing legibility. Fix: Line 55: self.place_in_area('scatter_points', 'D3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=55, object=scatter_points)
issues.resolution_note: Repositioned geometry cloud using place_in_area to D1-F3 area as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The mathematical summation symbol occupies the center-left grid, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 55: self.place_at_grid('math_symbol', 'B5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=55, object=math_symbol)
issues.resolution_note: Repositioned math symbol using place_at_grid to B5 as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Poor grid space utilization; elements are clustered too close to the text margin. Fix: Line 55: self.place_in_area('combined_group', 'D1', 'F3', scale_factor=0.7) (line=55, object=math_symbol_and_scatter)
issues.resolution_note: Grouped elements together and placed in D1-F3 using place_in_area for better space utilization.
